groups.name: thegentlemen
groups.about: The Gentlemen is a ransomware-as-a-service group that emerged in July–August 2025 and quickly claimed over 320 victims in 17+ countries. It offers affiliates a 90% revenue share and uses a Go-based locker against Windows, Linux, NAS, and BSD. A 2026 compromised C2 server revealed over 1,570 linked victims.

groups.name: qilin
groups.about: Qilin ransomware was first observed in July 2022. It is written in Golang and offers multiple encryption modes that the operator controls. The group uses double extortion, demanding payment for a decryptor and for not releasing stolen data.

groups.name: incransom
groups.about: INC Ransom is a prolific ransomware-as-a-service operation active since July 2023. It targets healthcare, government, education, and manufacturing in North America and Europe, with no sector excluded. It posted over 200 victims in 2025 alone.

groups.name: akira
groups.about: Akira reportedly emerged in March 2023 and has been speculated to have ties to the former Conti group. Its affiliates reportedly also work with Snatch and BlackByte. The first version was written in C++ and later versions in Rust. Initial access has involved brute-force attacks on Cisco VPNs and exploitation of two CVEs.

groups.name: silentransomgroup
groups.about: Silentransomgroup is described in the notes as a former Conti team, also tracked as Chatty Spider and UNC3753. The notes give no further details on its operations or targets.

groups.name: rhysida
groups.about: Rhysida is a ransomware-as-a-service group that emerged in May 2023. It uses phishing and Cobalt Strike to breach networks and deploy its payload. It threatens to publish stolen data, leaves PDF notes, and accepts Bitcoin. The notes say the ransomware is still in early development.

groups.name: medusalocker
groups.about: The notes describe Medusa as a DDoS bot written in .NET 2.0, not a ransomware group. Its current command-and-control uses HTTP, while its predecessor used IRC. The notes do not describe ransomware activity, so this entry may be mislabeled.

groups.name: lockbit5
groups.about: LockBit 5.0, also called ChuongDong, emerged in September 2025 after the February 2024 law enforcement takedown of LockBit. It introduced cross-platform payloads targeting Windows, Linux, and VMware ESXi. It continues the RaaS affiliate model of its predecessors.

groups.name: safepay
groups.about: SafePay emerged in September 2024 and grew rapidly while rejecting the RaaS model, running all operations in-house. It claimed over 300 victims worldwide by mid-2025. An early high-profile attack on UK telematics firm Microlise reportedly stole 1.2 TB of data.

groups.name: krybit
groups.about: Krybit is an emerging RaaS group that launched in late March 2026. It offers affiliates an 80/20 revenue split and encrypts Windows, Linux, ESXi, and NAS devices. It became known for a public feud with rival 0APT, with each group leaking the other's operator data.

groups.name: braincipher
groups.about: Brain Cipher emerged in July 2024 with both Windows and Linux variants. It reportedly uses a leaked LockBit Black build and is suspected of exploiting CVE-2023-28252. Demands start at $150,000 and are paid in Monero. In 2025 it moved its negotiation portal to a new server.

groups.name: metaencryptor
groups.about: Ransomware group first observed in mid-2023. Targets medium-to-large enterprises in legal, technology, logistics, manufacturing, and finance, mainly in the UK, Europe, and Southeast Asia. Uses AES-256 and RSA-2048 encryption with double extortion.

groups.name: payload
groups.about: Payload emerged in early 2026 and uses Babuk-derived source code to attack Windows and ESXi systems with double extortion. It targets healthcare, energy, real estate, and agriculture. It claimed 12 victims across seven countries within hours of launching its leak site.

groups.name: play
groups.about: Play ransomware, also called PlayCrypt, was first observed in June 2022 and uses double extortion. It has targeted many organizations in Latin America. Its initial access methods include phishing, exposed services, and valid account compromise. In 2023, Symantec reported its custom .NET data-enumeration and exfiltration tools.

groups.name: aurora
groups.about: Aurora is ransomware associated with a multi-purpose Go-based malware in use since mid-2022. Multiple criminal teams distribute it, and it is also sold on underground forums as an infostealer and botnet under the same name.

groups.name: everest
groups.about: Everest collects and analyzes information about its victims, focusing on customer privacy, financial data, databases, and credit card information. It leaks stolen data on the darknet. It threatens to leak data and keep victims' files if they do not make contact.
